# 3-Week Powerlifting Peaking Block

**Client Profile:** 28F, intermediate recreational lifter, 21 days to meet, post-accumulation block
**Goal:** Taper volume, maintain/sharpen intensity, peak fresh on meet day
**Structure:** 4 sessions/week (Mon, Wed, Fri, Sat), all percentages based on current training maxes (TM ≈ 95–97% of expected meet 1RM)

---

## Programming Philosophy

The first two weeks hold intensity in the 85–92.5% range while cutting working volume roughly 30% per week. Week 3 is a true taper with one heavy single mid-week, then full deload into meet day. We are not building anything new — we are sharpening, dialing in commands, and arriving recovered.

---

## WEEK 1 — Intensity Introduction, Moderate Volume

**Theme:** First exposure to opener-range weights. Tighten technique, no grinders. RPE cap 8.

### Monday — Squat / Bench Primary
- **Competition Squat:** Work up to 87.5% × 2, then 3 × 2 @ 85%
- **Competition Bench (paused, comp grip):** 90% × 1, then 4 × 2 @ 85%
- **Close-Grip Bench:** 3 × 5 @ RPE 7
- **Pendlay Row:** 3 × 6
- **Triceps pushdowns:** 3 × 10–12

### Wednesday — Deadlift Primary
- **Competition Deadlift:** Work up to 87.5% × 1, then 3 × 2 @ 82.5%
- **Pause Squat (2-count, mid-shin or just below parallel):** 4 × 3 @ 70%
- **Romanian Deadlift:** 3 × 6
- **Hanging knee raise:** 3 × 10

### Friday — Bench Volume / Squat Technique
- **Competition Bench:** 5 × 3 @ 80% (all paused)
- **Tempo Squat (3-count down):** 4 × 3 @ 70%
- **Spoto Press or Larsen Press:** 3 × 5
- **Lat pulldown:** 4 × 8
- **Rear delt flye:** 3 × 12

### Saturday — Heavy Single + Accessories
- **Competition Squat:** Single @ 90% (RPE 8 cap — leave clear room)
- **Competition Deadlift:** 3 × 3 @ 75%
- **Walking lunges:** 3 × 8/leg
- **Standing DB OHP:** 3 × 8
- **Plank:** 3 × 45s

**Recovery note:** 8+ hours sleep, full caloric maintenance, mobility 10 min/day. No new conditioning modalities.

---

## WEEK 2 — Peak Intensity Week

**Theme:** Heaviest training stimulus of the block. Hit opener and possibly second-attempt territory on each lift. RPE cap 8.5.

### Monday — Squat Heavy Single + Bench Volume
- **Competition Squat:** Work up to 92.5% × 1 (opener simulation, full commands — "squat," "rack")
- **Back-off Squat:** 2 × 2 @ 80%
- **Competition Bench:** 5 × 2 @ 82.5% (paused, commands)
- **Close-Grip Bench:** 2 × 5
- **Chest-supported row:** 3 × 8

### Wednesday — Deadlift Heavy Single
- **Competition Deadlift:** Work up to 92.5% × 1 (opener simulation, full "down" command)
- **Back-off Deadlift:** 2 × 2 @ 80%
- **Competition Squat:** 3 × 3 @ 75% (smooth, fast)
- **Hanging knee raise:** 3 × 10

### Friday — Bench Heavy Single
- **Competition Bench:** Work up to 92.5% × 1 (opener simulation, full "start, press, rack")
- **Back-off Bench:** 3 × 2 @ 82.5%
- **Tempo Squat:** 3 × 3 @ 65%
- **Lat pulldown:** 3 × 8
- **Triceps pushdown:** 3 × 12

### Saturday — Light Movement / Speed Work
- **Speed Squat:** 5 × 2 @ 65%
- **Speed Deadlift:** 4 × 1 @ 65%
- **Speed Bench:** 6 × 2 @ 60%
- Light back/abs, no failure

**Cue this week:** This is your hardest training session of the block. After Friday's bench single, the heavy lifting is essentially done. Everything from here forward is sharpening and recovery.

---

## WEEK 3 — Taper & Meet Week

**Theme:** Volume drops ~60% from Week 1. One last opener feel, then back off completely. Sleep, eat, hydrate.

### Monday (Day 7 out) — Final Heavy Touches
- **Competition Squat:** Work up to opener (90%) × 1, full commands
- **Competition Bench:** Work up to opener (90%) × 1, full commands
- Stop. No back-offs, no accessories beyond a few light pulldowns or band work if she wants.

### Wednesday (Day 5 out) — Deadlift Opener + Light Movement
- **Competition Deadlift:** Work up to opener (90%) × 1, full command
- **Bench:** 3 × 3 @ 60%, paused, crisp
- That's it.

### Friday (Day 3 out) — Final Primer
- **Squat:** 2 × 2 @ 60%
- **Bench:** 2 × 2 @ 60%
- **Deadlift:** 1 × 1 @ 60% (or skip — trainer's call based on how she feels)
- Total session under 30 minutes. Leave the gym wanting more.

### Saturday (Day 2 out) — Rest
Full rest. Light walk, mobility, mental rehearsal of attempts and commands.

### Sunday (Day 1 out / Meet Day Eve) — Rest
Travel, weigh-in if applicable, hydrate, normal carb intake, sleep early.

### MEET DAY
Warmups: empty bar → 40% × 5 → 60% × 3 → 75% × 2 → 85% × 1 → 92–94% × 1 → opener. Same ramp for each lift.

---

## Attempt Selection Guidance

- **Opener:** 90% of TM — should move like a warmup. Something she could hit 3x on her worst day.
- **Second:** ~95% of TM — confident PR territory or solid meet PR.
- **Third:** Based on how second moved. If bar speed was strong, +2.5–5 kg squat/DL, +1–2.5 kg bench. If it ground, repeat or take a small jump.

---

## Nutrition & Recovery Notes

**Weeks 1–2:** Maintenance calories, 1.8–2.2 g/kg protein, plenty of carbs around training. Don't cut weight if avoidable — if making weight, start water/sodium manipulation only in Week 3 per her federation rules.

**Week 3:** Maintain or slightly increase carbs. Sodium normal until protocol dictates otherwise. Sleep is the #1 recovery variable — 8.5–9 hours nightly if possible.

**Throughout block:**
- No new exercises, no maximal accessories
- No conditioning beyond easy walking
- Soft tissue work and mobility maintained, nothing aggressive in Week 3
- Caffeine: keep normal in Weeks 1–2; consider lowering slightly Week 3 so meet-day dose hits harder

---

## Red Flags to Adjust For

If any Week 2 heavy single grinds above RPE 9, stop that lift's heavy work for the week and cut the Week 3 opener touch on that lift to 85%. If she shows up Monday of Week 3 feeling beat up, drop the Monday session to 80% doubles and call it. Fresh > sharp, always, this close to the platform.

Let me know her current TMs and I'll plug exact loads into every session.

# Easy Aerobic Work — Recovery & Readiness Only

Adding light cardio to support recovery, blood flow, and meet-day readiness. Nothing that touches glycogen meaningfully or adds measurable fatigue. All sessions are nasal-breathing pace or Zone 1 (RPE 2–3, conversational, can hum a tune).

---

## Modality Options (client's preference)

- Incline treadmill walk (3–5% grade, 5–5.5 km/h)
- Outdoor walk
- Easy bike (flat road or stationary, light resistance)
- Easy elliptical

**Avoid:** running, rowing intervals, stairs, anything that loads the spine, hips, or shoulders in a fatiguing pattern. No HIIT, no "Z2 building" — this is purely recovery cardio.

---

## WEEK 1 — Recovery Cardio

- **Tuesday:** 20 min easy walk
- **Thursday:** 20 min easy walk or bike
- **Sunday:** 25–30 min easy walk (outdoors if possible — mental decompression)

Total: ~70 min easy aerobic across the week.

---

## WEEK 2 — Trim Slightly

- **Tuesday:** 15–20 min easy walk
- **Thursday:** 15 min easy walk or bike
- **Sunday:** 20 min easy walk

Total: ~50–55 min. Volume comes down with overall training stress.

---

## WEEK 3 — Meet Week (Blood Flow Only)

- **Tuesday (Day 6 out):** 15 min easy walk
- **Thursday (Day 4 out):** 10–15 min easy walk, optional
- **Saturday (Day 2 out):** 10–15 min easy walk — keeps her loose, not stiff from travel/rest
- **Sunday (Day 1 out):** 10 min very easy walk only if she feels stiff. Otherwise skip.

Total: 30–45 min, fully optional in the last 72 hours.

---

## Meet-Day Cardio Prep

About **30–45 min before warmups start**, a short general warmup primer:

- **5–8 min easy bike or walk** at very light intensity — just enough to raise core temperature, get a light sweat starting, and prime circulation
- Follow with her usual dynamic mobility flow (hips, T-spine, shoulders, ankles)
- Then into bar warmups for squat

Do not do this primer if the warmup room is hot/crowded and she's already warm from moving around. The goal is "warm and loose," not "winded."

---

## Rules for All Sessions

1. **Nasal breathing only.** If she has to open her mouth, slow down.
2. **No soreness, no cardio.** If she's beat up from a lifting session, skip it or just walk 10 minutes.
3. **Morning or post-lift, not pre-lift.** Never before a heavy session.
4. **Fasted or fed, doesn't matter** — pick what she tolerates.
5. **Stop if anything feels like effort.** This is not training.

---

## Why This Works

Light aerobic work on non-lifting days promotes recovery via increased blood flow without adding meaningful systemic fatigue or eating into glycogen. The taper of cardio volume mirrors the taper of lifting volume — both arrive at meet day minimized. The meet-day primer is the only "purposeful" cardio, and it's just to flip the switch from sitting around backstage to ready to squat.

If she normally does more cardio than this in daily life (active job, dog walks, etc.), count that toward the total and trim these sessions further. The number on the platform is what matters.

# Leave the Cue Alone — Mostly

Short answer: **don't introduce new technical work in a peaking block.** But there's nuance here worth unpacking.

---

## The Principle

Peaking blocks are for expression, not construction. Motor patterns under near-maximal loads should be automatic — the lifter's attention belongs on bracing, the commands, and bar path, not on actively reorganizing the upper back mid-setup. Adding cognitive load to a heavy lift in the final 3 weeks is a recipe for missed lifts, not better ones.

If the cue is **already working** for her — meaning her setup is tighter, the bar is moving well, no shoulder discomfort — keep using it as part of her normal setup routine. Just don't *drill* it as something new to fix.

---

## When to Leave It Completely Alone

- She's hitting her openers and second attempts smoothly with the cue
- Bar path is consistent
- No pain or weird pressing patterns
- She's confident with it

If all of these are true: it's part of her setup now. Treat it as routine, not a project.

---

## When It's Worth a Light Touch

If she's still **searching for the cue** under the bar — re-setting, taking too long, looking uncertain — that's a setup problem that will show up on the platform and get worse under meet-day adrenaline. In that case:

**Drill it only in warmups and submaximal sets, not at heavy singles.**

- Empty bar and 40–60% sets in Weeks 1–2: deliberately rehearse the upper back set — pull shoulder blades down and together, set them on the bench, *then* unrack. Make it part of the unrack sequence so it becomes automatic.
- By the time she's at 80%+, she should not be thinking about it — it should just happen.
- Week 3: zero technical cueing. Setup is whatever she's been doing. Trust it.

---

## A Caution on "More"

"Pull my shoulders together more" can quietly drift into over-retraction, which can actually hurt the press — it lifts the chest but can disconnect the lats, reduce leg drive transfer, and make the bar path inconsistent. Watch for:

- Elbows flaring more than usual
- Bar touching higher on the chest than her norm
- Loss of lat tightness off the chest

If you see any of those, the cue has gone too far. The fix is usually **"shoulders down and back into the bench,"** emphasizing the *down* (depression) over the *together* (retraction). Depression locks the lats in; retraction alone doesn't.

---

## My Recommendation for This Block

1. **Weeks 1–2 warmups (empty bar through ~70%):** Let her rehearse the cue deliberately as part of unrack routine. 2–3 reps thinking about it, then stop thinking.
2. **All working sets 80%+:** No technical cueing from you or her. Setup, breath, commands, press.
3. **Week 3:** Cue is invisible. She sets up the way she sets up. If she asks about it, tell her it looks good and to trust her setup.
4. **Watch for over-retraction** at heavier weights and intervene only if bar path or chest contact changes.

The meet is not the place to install technique. It's the place to express the technique she already has.

# Meet Day — Morning Through First Attempts

A meet day runs on rhythm. The lifter who eats, warms up, and attempts on a predictable cadence outperforms the one who's reacting to the clock all day. Here's the template — adjust times to her actual session start.

---

## Assumptions

- **Session start (first squat attempt of the flight):** let's call it 10:00 AM
- **Weigh-in:** 2 hours before, 8:00 AM (24-hour weigh-in federations: adjust accordingly)
- **She's not cutting weight** — if she is, the early hours change significantly and we'd plan separately

Shift everything below relative to her actual session start time.

---

## 5:30–6:00 AM — Wake Up

- Wake naturally if possible; alarm if not
- Light water with a pinch of salt (200–300 ml)
- Bathroom, brief mobility — 5 min of easy hip and shoulder circles, nothing structured
- No phone doom-scrolling. Calm morning.

---

## 6:00–7:30 AM — Pre-Weigh-In Window

If she's at weight already and not cutting:

- **Small first breakfast** around 6:00–6:30:
  - Something familiar she's eaten before training many times
  - Example: oatmeal with banana and honey, or toast with jam and a little protein (eggs or yogurt)
  - 300–500 calories, mostly carbs, moderate protein, low fat, low fiber
  - Coffee if she normally has coffee — same dose as a normal training day, no more
- Sip water steadily but don't chug

If she's cutting and just made weight, post weigh-in nutrition is a separate protocol — flag this and I'll write it out.

---

## 8:00 AM — Weigh-In

- In and out. Standard process.

---

## 8:00–8:45 AM — Second Breakfast / Top-Up

- **Second small meal** within 30 min of weigh-in:
  - Rice and chicken, bagel with turkey, oatmeal again — whatever sits well
  - 400–600 calories, again carb-dominant
- Continue sipping water + electrolytes (sodium especially)
- Get to the venue, find her rack/spot, lay out gear: singlet, belt, wrist wraps, shoes, knee sleeves, chalk, snacks, water

- Submit squat opener attempt card (most feds want this 15–30 min before the flight starts — confirm at the venue)
- Locate handler/coach, confirm warmup rack assignment
- Bathroom

Timing the warmup to land **the last warmup single 5–10 minutes before her opener** is the whole game. If the flight is moving fast, compress; if slow, stretch rest periods. Watch the flight, not the clock.

### General Warmup (5–8 min)
- Easy bike or walk — light sweat, no fatigue
- Dynamic mobility: hips, ankles, T-spine, shoulders
- A few bodyweight squats and good mornings

### Squat Bar Warmups
Working back from a 90% opener (adjust loads to her actual numbers):

| Set | Load | Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Empty bar | 5–8 | Groove |
| 2 | 40% | 5 | |
| 3 | 60% | 3 | Belt optional |
| 4 | 75% | 2 | Belt on, sleeves on |
| 5 | 85% | 1 | Full gear, full setup |
| 6 | 92–94% | 1 | Last warmup — should feel like the opener |

**Rest:** 2–3 min between early sets, 3–4 min between the top sets. Total warmup ≈ 30–40 min.

After the last warmup single, she sits, stays warm (layers on), sips water, and waits for her name in the lineup.

---

## ~10:00 AM — Squat Opener

- She has roughly **1 minute** from name called to the bar leaving the rack
- Coach calls her up when she's 2–3 lifters out
- She walks out, sets up, waits for "squat" command, executes, waits for "rack" command

### Between Squat Attempts
- 3 attempts per lifter, ~8–15 lifters per flight, so each lifter's attempts are roughly **8–15 minutes apart**
- Stay warm: jacket on, light movement between attempts, no sitting still for long
- Submit next attempt **within 1 minute of completing previous attempt** (rule varies — confirm)
- Small carb snack between rounds if appetite allows (rice cake, dates, gummies, sports drink)

---

## After Squats — Transition to Bench (typically 10–20 min break)

- Quick bathroom, fluids, small snack (~150–200 cal carbs)
- Mental reset — squats are done, whatever happened happened
- Begin bench warmup timed to land the last single ~5–10 min before her bench opener

### Bench Bar Warmups
Same ramp structure:

| Set | Load | Reps |
|---|---|---|
| Empty bar | × 8 (some pin to chest paused, some touch and go) | |
| 40% | × 5 | |
| 60% | × 3 (paused) | |
| 75% | × 2 (paused) | |
| 85% | × 1 (paused, full commands) | |
| 92–94% | × 1 (paused, full commands) | |

Practice the "start, press, rack" command sequence on the top 2 warmup singles. This is non-negotiable — these commands cost more lifters than the weight does.

---

## After Bench — Transition to Deadlift (typically 10–20 min break)

- Fluids, small carb snack
- Most lifters need slightly **more** time to warm into deadlifts — back tends to stiffen after sitting for bench
- Light walk, hip mobility, a few RDLs with the bar

### Deadlift Bar Warmups
Deadlifts use fewer warmup sets to save the back:

| Set | Load | Reps |
|---|---|---|
| Empty bar | × 5 (RDL-style) | |
| 50% | × 3 | |
| 70% | × 2 | |
| 82% | × 1 | |
| 90% | × 1 (full setup, wait for "down" command on lockout) | |

That's it. No more than 5–6 working warmup sets. Last single ~5–10 min before opener.

---

## Throughout the Day — Logistics

**Hydration:** Sip steadily. Don't slam water — she'll bloat and get sluggish. Aim for clear-pale urine all day.

**Food:** Small carb-dominant snacks every 45–90 min between flights. Examples: rice cakes with honey, dates, bananas, gummy bears, sports drink, white rice in a Tupperware. Avoid anything new, greasy, or high-fiber.

**Caffeine:** If she uses it, dose it twice — once before squats (~30 min prior) and a smaller top-up before deadlifts. Don't stack it; she'll crash.

**Warmth:** Hoodie, sweats, layers between attempts. Cold muscles miss lifts.

**Mental:** Headphones if she likes them. Avoid watching every other lifter — it's draining. Stay in her own bubble.

**Attempt selection:** Coach (you) makes the call on second and third attempts based on bar speed and how the previous attempt looked. She doesn't need to think about numbers — she just lifts what's loaded.

---

**Track the flight, not the clock.** Every warmup ramp is timed off how fast the lifters ahead of her are moving, not off the schedule printed in the morning. A coach or handler watching the flight and calling her warmups is worth 10 kg on the day.

If you want, I can also draft a printable single-page meet-day timing sheet she can keep in her gym bag.

# Reconsidering the Structure — Let's Talk About This First

Before I redraw the block, I want to flag a concern: **inserting a deload between Week 1 and Week 2 of a 3-week peak leaves only 1 hard week before the meet.** That can work, but it changes the shape of the peak significantly, and there's a better option worth considering.

---

## The Problem with a Mid-Peak Deload

The original block was already a taper — Week 1 was moderate, Week 2 was the peak intensity touch, Week 3 was deload into the meet. If we insert a deload between 1 and 2, the sequence becomes:

- Week 1 (moderate) → Deload → Week 2 (heavy singles) → Week 3 (meet taper)

That gives her **only one heavy exposure (Week 2)** before the meet, with a deload immediately before it. She'd come into the heavy singles fresh, which is good — but she'd then need to taper again immediately, which compresses the peak and risks her feeling flat on meet day from too much easy work in a row.

---

## What I'd Recommend Instead

If she's coming in beat up from accumulation, the better move is **to make Week 1 itself the deload**, then keep Weeks 2 and 3 as planned. This means:

- **Week 1 = deload/recovery** (was: moderate intensity)
- **Week 2 = heavy singles / peak intensity** (unchanged)
- **Week 3 = meet taper** (unchanged)

# Hold On — Let's Talk About This Before I Write It

I want to push back on this one before changing the program, because **95% singles on all three lifts mid-block is a meaningfully different ask than testing her opener**, and I don't think it's what she actually needs.

---

## The Core Issue

**A 95% single is not an opener test. It's a second-attempt simulation.**

Her opener should be ~90% of her training max, which is roughly 87–88% of her expected meet 1RM. The whole point of the opener is that it's a weight she could hit on her worst day — a layup. Testing it at 95% in training doesn't validate the opener; it validates a number she shouldn't be opening with.

If she hits a 95% single 9–10 days out from the meet, one of two things happens:

1. **It moves well** → she gets excited, wants to push her opener up, opens too heavy, and the meet day dominoes start falling.
2. **It grinds or misses** → her confidence is shot a week out, and she's now also carrying the fatigue of a max-effort single into the taper.

Neither serves her. And the original Week 2 already had **92.5% singles on all three lifts**, which is the correct opener simulation — heavy enough to rehearse commands and feel real weight, light enough to leave clear room and recover from in 7 days.

---

## What She's Probably Actually Asking For

When a lifter says "I want to test my opener," what they usually mean is one of these:

- **"I want confidence that my opener will move."** → The 92.5% single in Week 2 already does this. It's *heavier* than her opener will be on meet day relative to how she feels.
- **"I want to feel a heavier weight so the opener feels light."** → Valid instinct, but the cost is fatigue and miss risk. The 92.5% already accomplishes this — it's heavier than the opener.
- **"I want to know what my second attempt will feel like."** → This is the dangerous one. You don't need to know. Bar speed on the opener tells you and your coach what the second should be. Rehearsing it in training adds risk without adding information.

---

## What I'd Recommend Instead

**Keep the Week 2 singles at 92.5%, but make them feel like a real opener simulation.** That gives her the psychological win without the risk:

- Full warmup ramp, exactly as meet day
- Full gear: belt, sleeves, wrist wraps, shoes
- Full commands called by you or a training partner
- Treat the rack walkout, setup, and breath exactly as she will on the platform
- Film it so she can see the bar speed

A well-executed 92.5% single with full commands and gear will feel **bigger** than a sloppy 95% single done casually. The ritual is what builds confidence, not the load on the bar.

---

## If She Insists — The Compromise

If she's set on going heavier and you want to honor the request, here's what I'd accept, in order of preference:

### Option A (best): One lift only, 95%, squat or bench

Pick **one lift** — ideally squat or bench, not deadlift — and let her take a single at 95% on the Wednesday of Week 2. Keep the other two lifts at 92.5%. Rationale:

- Deadlift carries the highest systemic cost and the longest recovery time. A 95% pull 10 days out is the single highest-risk choice on this list. Avoid it.
- Squat or bench at 95%, done with full gear and commands, gives her the "I felt heavy weight" moment without trashing her CNS for all three lifts.

### Option B: All three at 93–94%, not 95%

Bump Week 2 singles from 92.5% to 93–94% across the board. This is barely different from the original plan, slightly more aggressive, still recoverable, and she gets to feel like she "went heavier."

### What I won't recommend
95% on all three lifts in the same week, 9–10 days out from a meet, on a lifter coming off a rough accumulation block (which is why we just turned Week 1 into a deload). **The math doesn't add up.** We deloaded Week 1 specifically because she was beat up. Stacking three near-max singles into Week 2 undoes that decision.

---

## My Honest Recommendation

Tell her: "Your Week 2 already has 92.5% singles on all three lifts with full commands and gear. That's your opener simulation, and it's heavier than what you'll open with. If you crush those and want to take one more single at 95% on squat or bench — your choice — we can talk about it the day of, based on how the 92.5% moved. But we're not programming three 95% singles in advance. That's not a peak, that's a mock meet, and we don't have time to recover from a mock meet."

That gives her agency, respects her input, and keeps the program intact.

# 48 Hours Before the Meet — Nutrition Protocol

Assuming **she's not cutting weight** (no water/sodium manipulation needed). If she is making weight, this protocol changes significantly — flag it and I'll rewrite. Times below assume a Sunday meet with a ~10 AM start; shift to match her actual schedule.

---

## Guiding Principles

1. **Nothing new.** Every food she eats in these 48 hours should be food she's eaten before training many times. The meet is not the place to try a new pre-workout meal.
2. **Carb-forward, moderate protein, low fat, low fiber as she gets closer.** Carbs top up glycogen; fat and fiber slow digestion and cause GI issues.
3. **Hydrate steadily, not in spikes.** Sipping all day beats chugging.
4. **Sodium up, not down.** Lifters often under-salt the day before a meet. Salt holds water in the blood, supports blood pressure under heavy lifts, and prevents cramping.

---

## FRIDAY (48–36 hours out) — Normal Eating, Slight Carb Lean

Treat Friday like a normal training day with a small carb bump. Nothing dramatic.

### Calories & Macros
- **Calories:** Maintenance. Don't overeat — she'll feel sluggish Saturday.
- **Carbs:** ~5–6 g/kg bodyweight (slight increase from her normal intake)
- **Protein:** 1.6–2.0 g/kg
- **Fat:** Normal, but skew lower if she normally eats high-fat
- **Fiber:** Normal Friday, start trimming Saturday

### Fluids
- **Water:** ~35–40 ml/kg bodyweight across the day, sipped steadily
- **Electrolytes:** Add an electrolyte drink or a pinch of salt to one or two meals

### Sodium
- **Target:** Normal-to-slightly-high. If she normally eats ~3 g sodium/day, aim for ~4 g Friday. Salt food liberally.

### Practical Day
- Normal breakfast, lunch, dinner
- Add a carb snack mid-afternoon and before bed (rice cakes with honey, oatmeal, fruit)
- Last meal 2–3 hours before sleep
- **Bed early.** Friday sleep matters more than Saturday sleep (research consistently shows sleep two nights out predicts performance better than the night before).

---

## SATURDAY (Day Before) — Carb Load, Hydrate, Salt

This is the most important nutrition day of the block. Goal: top off muscle and liver glycogen, arrive at the venue Sunday morning hydrated and salted, no GI surprises.

### Calories & Macros
- **Calories:** Maintenance + 200–400 kcal from carbs. Not a true "carb load" (that's for endurance) — just a top-off.
- **Carbs:** ~7–8 g/kg bodyweight. Example: 60 kg lifter = 420–480 g carbs across the day.
- **Protein:** 1.6 g/kg (slightly lower than normal — protein is filling and crowds out carbs)
- **Fat:** Low. ~0.6–0.8 g/kg. Avoid fried food, heavy sauces, lots of cheese, nuts.
- **Fiber:** **Cut significantly.** Aim for under 20 g across the day. Switch to white rice, white bread, peeled fruit, low-fiber cereal. Skip salads, beans, lentils, raw cruciferous veg, high-fiber bars.

### Fluids
- **Water:** ~40 ml/kg, sipped across the entire day. Pale yellow urine all day = correct.
- **Add electrolytes** to at least 1–2 of those fluid intakes — sports drink, electrolyte tablet, or DIY (water + pinch of salt + splash of juice).
- **Stop large fluid intake by ~8 PM** to avoid waking up to pee.

### Sodium
- **Target:** ~5 g sodium across the day (roughly 12.5 g of table salt total, including what's in food).
- Salt every meal generously. Add salt to water bottles. Pretzels, salted rice cakes, soy sauce, pickles, broth — all useful.
- This is the single most under-done variable for non-cutting lifters. Don't skip it.

### Sample Saturday Meals (~60 kg lifter, ~2200 kcal)

**Breakfast (8 AM):** Oatmeal (80 g dry) with banana, honey, small amount of whey. Pinch of salt in the oats. Coffee. Water.

**Snack (10:30 AM):** Bagel with jam, salted. Sports drink.

**Lunch (1 PM):** White rice (150 g cooked weight × 2), grilled chicken (150 g), small amount of sauce, salted. Water with electrolyte tab.

**Snack (4 PM):** Rice cakes with honey, banana. Water.

**Dinner (7 PM):** White rice or pasta (large portion), lean protein (chicken, white fish, or lean ground turkey), cooked low-fiber veg (zucchini, carrots — well-cooked), salted generously. Small dessert if she wants — sorbet, plain cookies.

**Pre-bed (9 PM):** Small carb snack — toast with jam, or a few rice cakes. Sip water, not chug.

### Saturday Don'ts
- No alcohol
- No new restaurants or new foods
- No high-fiber "healthy" choices — save them for after the meet
- No giant late dinner — she'll sleep poorly
- No fasting or skipping meals to "feel light"

---

## SATURDAY NIGHT — Sleep

- In bed by 9:30–10:00 PM, lights out
- Cool, dark room
- No caffeine after ~2 PM Saturday
- If she's anxious and can't sleep: that's normal, don't catastrophize it. **Friday's sleep is the one that matters most for Sunday performance.** Tell her this in advance so she's not lying awake panicking about lying awake.

---

## SUNDAY MORNING — Meet Day (covered earlier, summarized here)

### 5:30–6:00 AM — Wake
- Water with pinch of salt (300 ml)

### 6:00–6:30 AM — First Breakfast
- 300–500 kcal, carb-dominant, low fat, low fiber, familiar
- Example: oatmeal + banana + honey, or white toast + jam + small protein
- Coffee at normal dose
- Sip water + electrolytes

### 8:00–8:45 AM — Second Breakfast / Top-Up
- 400–600 kcal, carb-dominant
- Example: bagel with turkey, or rice + chicken
- Continue sipping water + electrolytes

### Throughout the Meet
- Small carb snacks every 45–90 min: rice cakes, dates, gummies, sports drink, banana, white rice
- Sip water + electrolytes steadily; don't chug
- Caffeine dose ~30 min before squats, smaller top-up before deadlifts if she uses it

## Red Flags to Address

- **She's bloated/heavy Saturday night:** Slightly too much volume of food or fiber. Trim Sunday breakfast portion, prioritize liquid carbs (sports drink, juice) over solid.
- **She wakes up Sunday flat or dehydrated:** Sodium was too low Saturday, or fluids tapered too early. Add a salty broth + sports drink first thing Sunday.
- **GI issues Saturday night or Sunday AM:** Fiber wasn't cut enough, or she ate something unfamiliar. Sunday breakfast becomes white rice + a small amount of plain protein only.
- **She's nervous and not hungry Sunday AM:** Liquid calories. Sports drink, juice, a smoothie with banana and honey. Something is better than nothing — aim for at least 60–80 g carbs in the first meal even if it's all liquid.

# 3-Week Peaking Block — Final Consolidated Programme

**Client Profile:** 28F, intermediate recreational lifter, 21 days to meet, coming off a rough accumulation block
**Goal:** Recover from accumulation, sharpen on heavy singles, arrive fresh and confident on meet day
**Structure:** 4 lifting sessions/week (Mon, Wed, Fri, Sat), supplemented with light aerobic recovery work
**Loading basis:** All percentages based on current training maxes (TM ≈ 95–97% of expected meet 1RM)

---

## Programming Overview

| Week | Theme | Volume | Intensity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Recovery deload — flush accumulation fatigue | Low | Low (≤75%) |
| 2 | Peak intensity — opener simulation under full commands | Moderate | High (92.5%, with option for one 95% single) |
| 3 | Meet taper — final touches, then rest | Very low | Opener touch only |

The shape: arrive at Week 2 fresh, hit one clean heavy week, taper into the platform.

---

## WEEK 1 — Recovery Deload

**Theme:** Flush fatigue from accumulation. Keep movement patterns. Everything feels easy. RPE cap 6–7.

### Monday — Squat / Bench Light
- **Competition Squat:** Work up to 70% × 2, then 3 × 2 @ 70%
- **Competition Bench (paused, comp grip):** 4 × 3 @ 70%
- **Lat pulldown:** 3 × 10
- **Triceps pushdown:** 2 × 12

### Tuesday — Cardio
- 20 min easy walk (nasal breathing, RPE 2–3)

### Wednesday — Deadlift Light
- **Competition Deadlift:** Work up to 70% × 1, then 2 × 2 @ 70%
- **Pause Squat:** 3 × 3 @ 60%
- **Hanging knee raise:** 3 × 10

### Thursday — Cardio
- 20 min easy walk or bike

### Friday — Bench / Squat Touch
- **Competition Bench:** 4 × 2 @ 75% (paused, practice commands)
- **Tempo Squat (3-count down):** 3 × 3 @ 60%
- **Chest-supported row:** 3 × 8

### Saturday — Optional Light Movement
If recovered: speed work — 4 × 2 squat @ 60%, 4 × 2 bench @ 60%. If still beat up: **skip entirely**, walk and stretch.

### Sunday — Cardio
- 25–30 min easy walk, outdoors if possible

**Week 1 Checks (by Sunday evening):** Should feel fresh, slightly under-trained, sleeping well, normal appetite, no nagging joint issues. If still beat up: extend deload 3–4 days and cap Week 2 singles at 87.5%.

---

## WEEK 2 — Peak Intensity

**Theme:** Heaviest training stimulus of the block. Opener simulation under full gear, full commands. RPE cap 8.5. One optional 95% single on either squat or bench (lifter's choice, made the day of based on how the 92.5% moved). **No 95% deadlift** — recovery cost is too high this close to the meet.

### Monday — Squat Heavy Single + Bench Volume
- **Competition Squat:** Work up to 92.5% × 1 (opener simulation — full gear, full commands "squat / rack")
  - *Optional:* if 92.5% moved fast and she wants to test heavier, take one additional single at 95%. Coach's call.
- **Back-off Squat:** 2 × 2 @ 80%
- **Competition Bench:** 5 × 2 @ 82.5% (paused, commands)
- **Close-Grip Bench:** 2 × 5
- **Chest-supported row:** 3 × 8

### Tuesday — Cardio
- 15–20 min easy walk

### Wednesday — Deadlift Heavy Single
- **Competition Deadlift:** Work up to 92.5% × 1 (opener simulation — full "down" command). **Cap here. No 95%.**
- **Back-off Deadlift:** 2 × 2 @ 80%
- **Competition Squat:** 3 × 3 @ 75% (smooth, fast)
- **Hanging knee raise:** 3 × 10

### Thursday — Cardio
- 15 min easy walk or bike

### Friday — Bench Heavy Single
- **Competition Bench:** Work up to 92.5% × 1 (opener simulation, full "start / press / rack")
  - *Optional:* if she didn't take a 95% squat single Monday and wants the heavier touch here, take one single at 95%. **Pick one lift only — squat OR bench — not both.**
- **Back-off Bench:** 3 × 2 @ 82.5%
- **Tempo Squat:** 3 × 3 @ 65%
- **Lat pulldown:** 3 × 8
- **Triceps pushdown:** 3 × 12

### Saturday — Speed Work
- **Speed Squat:** 5 × 2 @ 65%
- **Speed Deadlift:** 4 × 1 @ 65%
- **Speed Bench:** 6 × 2 @ 60%
- Light back/abs, no failure

### Sunday — Cardio
- 20 min easy walk

**Technical Cueing Note:** In warmups (empty bar through ~70%), let her rehearse the shoulder set as part of her unrack routine — emphasizing "shoulders **down** and back into the bench," not just "together." At 80%+, zero technical cueing from coach or self. Setup is automatic. Watch for over-retraction at heavier weights (elbows flaring, bar touching too high, lat tightness lost off the chest) — intervene only if bar path changes.

---

## WEEK 3 — Meet Taper

**Theme:** Volume drops ~60% from Week 2. Final opener touches, then full deload. Sleep, eat, hydrate.

### Monday (Day 7 out) — Final Heavy Touches
- **Competition Squat:** Work up to opener (~90%) × 1, full commands
- **Competition Bench:** Work up to opener (~90%) × 1, full commands
- No back-offs. Optional light pulldowns or band work if she wants.

### Tuesday (Day 6 out) — Cardio
- 15 min easy walk

### Wednesday (Day 5 out) — Deadlift Opener + Light Bench
- **Competition Deadlift:** Work up to opener (~90%) × 1, full command
- **Bench:** 3 × 3 @ 60%, paused, crisp
- Done.

### Thursday (Day 4 out) — Cardio (optional)
- 10–15 min easy walk

### Friday (Day 3 out) — Final Primer
- **Squat:** 2 × 2 @ 60%
- **Bench:** 2 × 2 @ 60%
- **Deadlift:** 1 × 1 @ 60% (or skip — coach's call)
- Under 30 minutes total. Leave wanting more.

### Saturday (Day 2 out) — Rest + Carb Load
- Optional 10–15 min easy walk if stiff
- Full rest from lifting
- Carb-load and hydration day (see nutrition section)
- In bed by 9:30–10 PM

### Sunday (Day 1 out / Travel) — Rest
- Optional 10 min walk only if stiff
- Travel, normal eating, hydrate, mental rehearsal of attempts and commands
- Early sleep

### MEET DAY
See full meet-day protocol below.

---

## Cardio Programme Summary

All cardio is nasal-breathing, RPE 2–3, conversational pace. Modality: incline walk, outdoor walk, easy bike, or easy elliptical. **No running, rowing intervals, stairs, or anything spinal-loaded.**

| Week | Total weekly cardio |
|---|---|
| 1 | ~70 min across Tue / Thu / Sun |
| 2 | ~50 min across Tue / Thu / Sun |
| 3 | 30–45 min across Tue / Thu / Sat, fully optional |

**Rules:** Nasal breathing only. No cardio if sore or beat up. Never before a heavy lifting session. Stop if anything feels like effort.

---

## Attempt Selection

- **Opener:** ~90% of TM. Should move like a warmup — something she could hit 3× on her worst day.
- **Second:** ~95% of TM. Confident PR or solid meet PR.
- **Third:** Based on bar speed of the second. Strong speed: +2.5–5 kg squat/DL, +1–2.5 kg bench. Grindy: repeat or small jump.

Coach makes the call on attempts 2 and 3. Lifter doesn't think about numbers — she just lifts what's loaded.

---

## Nutrition & Recovery — Block-Wide

### Weeks 1–2
- Maintenance calories, 1.8–2.2 g/kg protein, carbs around training
- Don't cut weight if avoidable
- 8.5–9 hours sleep nightly is the #1 recovery variable
- No new exercises, no maximal accessories, no aggressive soft tissue work in Week 3
- Caffeine normal Weeks 1–2; consider lowering slightly in Week 3 so meet-day dose hits harder

### Meet Week — 48 Hours Before

Assumes she's **not cutting weight**. If cutting, separate protocol required.

**FRIDAY (48–36 hrs out) — Normal eating, slight carb lean**
- Calories: maintenance
- Carbs: ~5–6 g/kg
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg
- Fat: normal-low
- Fiber: normal
- Water: ~35–40 ml/kg, sipped steadily
- Sodium: ~4 g (salt food liberally)
- **Bed early** — Friday sleep matters more than Saturday sleep

**SATURDAY (Day Before) — Carb top-off, hydrate, salt**
- Calories: maintenance + 200–400 kcal from carbs
- Carbs: ~7–8 g/kg
- Protein: 1.6 g/kg
- Fat: low (~0.6–0.8 g/kg)
- Fiber: **under 20 g** — switch to white rice, white bread, peeled fruit
- Water: ~40 ml/kg, taper large intake after 8 PM
- Sodium: ~5 g — salt every meal, add to water bottles, use pretzels/broth/pickles
- **Nothing new, no alcohol, no giant late dinner**

Sample Saturday for ~60 kg lifter (~2200 kcal):
- **Breakfast:** Oatmeal + banana + honey + whey, salted, coffee
- **Snack:** Bagel + jam, sports drink
- **Lunch:** White rice (large) + grilled chicken, salted
- **Snack:** Rice cakes + honey + banana
- **Dinner:** White rice or pasta + lean protein + cooked low-fiber veg, salted
- **Pre-bed:** Toast + jam, sip water

### Quick Reference Card

| Variable | Friday | Saturday | Sunday AM |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calories | Maintenance | +200–400 | Two small meals, ~800–1100 total |
| Carbs (g/kg) | 5–6 | 7–8 | High, spread across snacks |
| Protein (g/kg) | 1.6–2.0 | 1.6 | Moderate |
| Fat | Normal-low | Low | Very low |
| Fiber | Normal | <20 g | Minimal |
| Water (ml/kg) | 35–40 | 40, taper after 8 PM | Sip, don't chug |
| Sodium | ~4 g | ~5 g | Continue salting |
| New foods | No | No | Absolutely not |

---

## MEET DAY — Full Protocol

Times assume a 10 AM session start. Shift to match her actual start.

### 5:30–6:00 AM — Wake
- Water with pinch of salt (300 ml)
- 5 min easy mobility
- No phone scrolling

### 6:00–6:30 AM — First Breakfast
- 300–500 kcal, carb-dominant, low fat, low fiber, familiar
- Example: oatmeal + banana + honey, or white toast + jam + small protein
- Coffee at normal dose
- Sip water + electrolytes

### 8:00 AM — Weigh-In

### 8:00–8:45 AM — Second Breakfast
- 400–600 kcal, carb-dominant
- Example: bagel + turkey, or rice + chicken
- Continue water + electrolytes
- Get to venue, lay out gear

### 8:45–9:00 AM — Logistics
- Submit squat opener card
- Locate handler, confirm warmup rack
- Bathroom

### 9:00 AM — Begin Squat Warmup (target last single ~5–10 min before opener)

**General warmup (5–8 min):** Easy bike or walk, dynamic mobility, bodyweight squats and good mornings.

**Squat bar warmups:**
| Set | Load | Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Empty bar | 5–8 | Groove |
| 2 | 40% | 5 | |
| 3 | 60% | 3 | Belt optional |
| 4 | 75% | 2 | Belt on, sleeves on |
| 5 | 85% | 1 | Full gear |
| 6 | 92–94% | 1 | Full setup, like the opener |

Rest 2–3 min early, 3–4 min top sets. **Track the flight, not the clock.**

### ~10:00 AM — Squat Opener
- Stay warm between attempts (jacket, light movement)
- Small carb snack between rounds (rice cake, dates, gummies, sports drink)
- Submit next attempt within 1 minute

### After Squats — Transition to Bench (~10–20 min)
- Bathroom, fluids, ~150–200 kcal carbs
- Mental reset

**Bench bar warmups:**
| Set | Load | Reps |
|---|---|---|
| Empty bar | 8 (mix paused & TNG) | |
| 40% | 5 | |
| 60% | 3 (paused) | |
| 75% | 2 (paused) | |
| 85% | 1 (paused, full commands) | |
| 92–94% | 1 (paused, full commands) | |

Practice "start / press / rack" on top 2 warmup singles. **Commands cost more lifters than weight does.**

### After Bench — Transition to Deadlift (~10–20 min)
- Fluids, small carb snack
- Light walk, hip mobility, a few RDLs with empty bar — back stiffens after sitting

**Deadlift bar warmups (fewer sets, save the back):**
| Set | Load | Reps |
|---|---|---|
| Empty bar | 5 (RDL-style) | |

## Red Flags & Adjustments

- **Week 2 single grinds above RPE 9:** Stop that lift's heavy work for the week. Cut Week 3 opener touch on that lift to 85%.
- **Monday of Week 3 feels beat up:** Drop session to 80% doubles and call it. Fresh > sharp.
- **Saturday night bloated/heavy:** Too much food volume or fiber. Sunday breakfast smaller, lean on liquid carbs (sports drink, juice).
- **Wakes up Sunday flat/dehydrated:** Sodium was too low Saturday. Salty broth + sports drink first thing.
- **GI issues Sat night or Sun AM:** Fiber wasn't cut enough. Sunday breakfast = white rice + plain protein only.
- **Nervous and not hungry Sunday AM:** Liquid calories. Smoothie with banana and honey, sports drink. At least 60–80 g carbs in the first meal even if all liquid.
- **Can't sleep Saturday night:** Normal. Friday's sleep is the one that matters most. Tell her this in advance.
